title: Offline-first prompt bundling & progressive hydration — personal scratchpad
content:
Notes to self:

This is a rough design sketch for a client-side protocol that bundles multiple small prompts/utterances into a single prefetchable artifact (a "bundle") and then progressively hydrates/streams full model outputs when the user actually needs them. Goal is to lower tail latency and save tokens for repetitive micro-interactions in mobile/edge offline-first flows.

High-level goals:
- Make short-turn interactions (typing/autocomplete, micro-prompts) feel instant even on flaky networks.
- Reduce duplicate tokens sent to server for repeated context that is shared across nearby events.
- Support offline-friendly caching & background prefetch (respecting privacy flags).
- Allow graceful degradation: serve cached or partial hydration if the network is slow.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Clients can persist small encrypted bundles locally (per-user).
- Server exposes a lightweight bundle submission/lookup API.
- Bundles have a version+schema, can be invalidated by the server.
- Privacy: users can mark bundles non-prefetchable (sensitive).

Basic API shape (sketch):
- POST /v1/bundles -> returns bundle_id, summary_hash, eligibility_flags
- GET /v1/bundles/{bundle_id}/preview -> small summary, token_estimate, eligible_for_prefetch
- POST /v1/bundles/{bundle_id}/hydrate?mode=progressive -> opens SSE or WebSocket stream that sends progressive sections
- GET /v1/bundles/lookup?client_sig=XXX -> server-side heuristic to match existing bundles for a client

Bundle model (text representation):
- bundle_id: uuid
- schema_version: 1
- created_by: client-id
- entries: [ {entry_id, role, text, embeddings_hash, meta_tags } ]
- summary: short text synthesized on submit for quick matching
- prefetch_flags: [low_priority, background_ok, sensitive_no_prefetch]
- expire_at: ISO timestamp

Example (as text):
{
  "bundle_id": "b1f2d...",
  "schema_version": "1",
  "entries": [
    {"entry_id":"e1","role":"user","text":"Search my notes for "invoice"","meta_tags":["search","personal"]},
    {"entry_id":"e2","role":"system","text":"recent-context: last-5-utterances"}
  ],
  "summary": "note-search + recent context",
  "prefetch_flags": ["background_ok"]
}

Progressive hydration modes (sketch):
- immediate-preview: server returns a compact result (one-shot) with short answer (<= 64 tokens) suitable for UI preview.
- progressive-steps: server streams first the high-confidence sentence(s) then lower-confidence expansions. Good for streaming UI with optimistic display.
- full-lazy: server returns a pointer and hydrates only when client explicitly requests the expanded entry.

Client state machine (ASCII):

[idle] -> (collect events) -> [collecting] -> (threshold reached or trigger) -> [bundling] -> (POST /bundles) -> [cached]
[cached] -> (background prefetch allowed) -> [prefetching] -> (prefetch success or fail) -> [serving]
[serving] -> (user needs expansion) -> [hydrating] -> (progressive stream) -> [serving-expanded]

Notes: triggers = typing pause, app background, explicit user action (e.g., long-press), scheduler window. Thresholds: token_count, elapsed_time, event_count.

Hydration stream layout (SSE/WebSocket frames):
- frame(type=meta, bundle_id, entry_id, approx_tokens)
- frame(type=partial, text_chunk, confidence_est)
- frame(type=delta_token, token, token_index)
- frame(type=done, stats)
- frame(type=fallback, reason)

Config knobs to expose to apps (client-side + server-based defaults):
- max_bundle_tokens: 1024 (client cap)
- max_entries_per_bundle: 12
- background_prefetch_window_secs: 30
- hydration_granularity: [sentence, clause, token]
- allow_stale_preview: true
- prefetch_strategy: [aggressive|opportunistic|disabled]
- privacy_policy: [allow_prefetch, deny_prefetch, prompt_user]

Cache / eviction policy (client):
- LRU by last_used + sensitivity score.
- Soft TTL from server expire_at; hard TTL local max 30d.
- On low storage, drop largest bundles first (by tokens) unless ttl < 24h.

Server heuristics for bundling acceptance:
- Reject if embedding_hash collision or schema mismatch.
- Prefer bundling similar client histories (fingerprint summary).
- Tag bundles as "globalizable" (safe to precompute) vs "local-only" (must not be shared across devices).

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- What is a safe default for background_prefetch_window on mobile (battery + data)? 15s vs 30s vs 60s?
- How to account for model-version drift: server must invalidate or mark stale when model weight updates cause regressions. Do we epoch bundles per model_version? (probably yes)
- Security: if bundles are stored on device and encrypted, how to handle key rotation? KMS vs local device key?
- UX: how to signal "partial/hydrated" responses cleanly without jarring reflows? (suggest: replace-on-complete with small crossfade)
- Billing/metrics: how to attribute tokens consumed during background prefetch vs user-triggered hydration? Need token tagging and offline accounting.

Performance considerations:
- Bundling can reduce duplicate context tokens sent to the server; but increases average request size. Measure 95th percentile RTT for small-interaction flows to ensure we don't worsen tail latency.
- Progressive hydration over cellular should fallback to previews if bandwidth low. Implement client-side backpressure for hydration streams.

Edge cases / failure modes:
- Stale bundle matches -> show preview with explicit "refresh" affordance.
- Partial hydration aborted -> keep preview cached and queue rehydrate when connectivity improves.
- Conflicting edits for collaborative flows -> bundle should be single-user by default, collaborative bundles require server coordination and optimistic merging.

Implementation TODOs (short roadmap):
- Prototype API + in-memory server: accept bundles, serve preview and progressive stream (2 sprint spike).
- Android/iOS client integration sample: local store + background prefetch worker (1 sprint each).
- Add telemetry: prefetch_success_rate, hydration_latency_p50/p95, bytes_prefetched, tokens_wasted_by_prefetch.
- UX experiment A/B toggles for prefetch_strategy set to opportunistic vs disabled.

Next immediate steps (my action items):
- Wire up a minimal server mock (Node/Express) that accepts POST /bundles and streams progressive hydration from a canned model output. (Ethan can help with streaming infra.)
- Draft a short Confluence page with the API shape and diagrams (we have a placeholder in linked_artifacts).
- Run quick product interview with Maya to validate privacy defaults and UX for preview vs hydrated answer.

References and quick links:
- Related: offline-first caching experiments in mobile-apps (internal), prefetched embeddings discussion in GH PR 561.
- Metrics: see spreadsheet "client-prefetch-capacity.xlsx" in product folder (todo: link).

Rough notes / heuristics to remember: quantify tokens saved per session; prefer small many bundles over one huge monolith; prefer background prefetch only when device is on WiFi and charging if privacy allows.

Random thought: could we store a tiny neural sketch (compressed embedding + compact summary) on-device and use it for super-fast local hints (no hydration) for trivial queries? If good, surface as "instant-preview" and reduce server hits massively.

End of scratchpad.

-- sm
